searchText: Not promising anything but I am thinking about this problem 🙂 Awesome, even if it's rough and not fully thought through, posting a write-up of your thoughts at whatever point you are ready would be really helpful. Also, I don't think there's been a good summary of what was talked about at the summit so we should also focus on getting that done just to capture what has already been discussed. Quick summary from memory: 1. Do we do witness gas accounting by dumb repricing of witness-heavy operations, eg. https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/protocol-changes-to-bound-witness-size/3885 , or do we explicitly charge per byte or per hash? 2. If the latter, do we charge at time the opcode is executed, or do we store it in a counter and charge at the end of transaction execution? In practice, this generally means, how much do we care about preserving the ability for contract A to call contract B without "trusting" B with the ability to cause the entire tx to fail? This was expressed at the summit in terms of four options, but this is roughly how it breaks down in practice
